title: Joules per Decision: Measuring the Energy Cost of LLM Agents in Network Operations — measurement code and results
description:
Measurement code, per-task result files, run logs, and analysis scripts accompanying the paper Joules per Decision: Measuring the Energy Cost of LLM Agents in Network Operations.

GPU board power is sampled at 10 Hz with a streaming nvidia-smi process and integrated over wall-clock time, net of a per-cell idle baseline, while four Qwen2.5 sizes perform subnet arithmetic, ACL rule evaluation, and BGP best-path selection, on a datacenter accelerator and an edge-class card, and on the NetArena benchmark.

The deposit includes the power sampler, the task generator and its grading function, an independent re-derivation of all 120 ground truths, the grading-rule audit, the statistical analyses, and the figure-generation code. scripts/validation/verify_deposit.py recomputes the paper's headline statistics from the result files and compares them against the printed values.

This version adds three experiments that the first deposit predates: the cost of agentic iteration, measured with a validator derived from the prompt rather than from the ground truth, so that the loop is blind to correctness in the way a real deployment is; a three-arm serving-framework comparison that separates a newer software stack from vLLM's continuous batching instead of confounding them; and four-bit NF4 quantization on the edge card. Both runs of the serving sweep are kept, from a cold and a hot card, so the agreement quoted for the thermal-drift flags can be recomputed.

All energy figures are GPU board power only; host, power-supply, cooling, and facility overheads are outside the instrument.
